producer_report.summary: Added one shared budget reserve and made a short job stop before any spend. Root cause: the budget was checked only per invocation, after reading and planning had spent, and the reserve left out the critic and later planning rounds. `reading::budget_reserve(config, stage)` is now the only place the caps are added. All caps come from config. At admission it is the reader, plus max_rounds × (planner + critic) when `[job_plan]` is enabled, plus the producer and verifier (10.00 with the shipped caps). Later stages count only what is still to run: Dispatch{planned}, Planner{round}, Critic{round} and Run. `Athena::preflight` applies it and returns a typed `BudgetShort` that names the shortfall, the reserve and the `[budget] job_usd` line in athena.toml. Call sites: `first_reading` (admission, and a queued job's re-read with its prior spend), `retry` (judged on its own spend, starting at 0), `dispatch` (before any commit, and the Run stage after planning), and the planner and critic checks in run/planning.rs. The drain maps `BudgetShort` to a held item: one `item <id> is left queued: ...` note, outcome `budget short`, not a failure, and the next item runs. I added `Read.held` for this. New tests: core arithmetic and shipped-config tests, an admission test (8.00 refused, zero driver invocations), a real-round critic table, a dispatch hold, a retry test, and a drain test. A CHANGELOG entry names the root cause and the three jobs. I ran the full suite in pieces, not as one run. The one-shot `cargo test --locked` I started in the background hit its time limit and was killed. The pieces were athena-core lib, the athena-core integration tests, all of athena-cli, athena-cap-change, athena-cap-study and xtask, and all passed. I did not run athena-data, athena-context, athena-score, athena-agent, athena-gate or athena-git (untouched). `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are clean.

open_issues: Plan departure: the lifecycle.rs edit is job_usd 5.60 with the scenario cost 0.7, not 5.60 alone. With 5.60 and cost 0.4 the job clears dispatch (5.20 left against 5.00 needed), so the test's expected refusal never happened. Both are numbers, and no assertion changed.

Plan departure: tests/drain.rs is not a listed deliverable, but `Read` gained a `held` field and two struct literals there (the Stub's `read` and the parallel Shared's `read`) needed `held: false`. A compile fix with no behavior change.

Plan departure: the drain test's premise was wrong. `athena.queue` makes no reader call and spends nothing. The test instead uses the reader failing on its first drain read ($0.60), so the drain's second read of the same item reaches admission with 0.60 prior spend. Request texts carry an acceptance bullet so the drain's own planning pass does not read them first.

The Run-stage hold from `go` carries the label `budget short` as a reason prefix, which `run_job` checks, because a new `Run` field would have broken the existing exhaustive Run literal in tests/drain.rs. A typed field would be cleaner if edits to that file are acceptable.

Dispatch counts the planning terms for a job that resumes from a kept candidate (no planner or producer runs), so such a resume can be held with less than the planning reserve left. This is the over-reserving the plan accepted; no existing test hit it.
`correct` (re-reading a proposed job) does not call the preflight; the brief names admission, retry, dispatch and per-round checks only.
A non-retryable job with a short budget now reports the budget shortfall from `retry`'s early preflight rather than 'not retryable'. No existing test asserted the other wording.
mistakes: My first drain test used plain requests with no acceptance bullet, so the drain's planning pass read item A ahead and consumed the scripted failing reader call; the item was 'not worked' instead of held. I rewrote the requests.
My first retry test failed because the scripted reader's summary did not name the retried job; fixed in the cost wrapper.
clippy's collapsible-if flagged the first version of the drain test's script; collapsed.
learnings: `athena.queue` (ask --later) makes no reader call; a queued item is read by the drain's `go`, and the drain's own planning pass reads a queued request first if its words leave the plan without acceptance. A drain test of the read path needs a request with an acceptance bullet.
The fake agent driver enforces no per-role cap and does not clamp a turn's cost_usd, so tests can make a planner turn cost more than planner_usd.
A reading of a retry is refused unless its summary, assumptions or criteria name the retried job, so a retry test's scripted reader must put the job id in its summary.
`RETRY_PREFIX` (`try again on `) is private to reading.rs. Test scripts match the literal text.
Adding a field to `drain::Read` or `drain::Run` breaks struct literals in tests/drain.rs, and every `Read {` literal in the repo is listed above; `Read` and `Run` derive Default.

The shipped athena.toml has [job_plan] enabled with 0.75/0.75/3 rounds. The core pin tests, run/tests.rs repo_with_config and cli test_config strip it; tests that want planning append their own section.
